why.role_legibility: D420 marks values (#sales, あなた) in a heavier/bolder weight than their gray labels (宛先, 差出人), giving a weight+color cue instead of color/opacity alone; 14AA and F516 distinguish label from value with color/brightness only (gray label, plain white value, same weight), which is legible but a slightly weaker cue — 14AA and F516 look identical to me on this axis so their order is a coin flip.
why.visual_craft: D420 puts the external-share warning on its own line with a directional arrow glyph (↗) instead of plain colored text sharing the header line, and pairs that with the bolder value weighting — small touches that read as more deliberate typographic craft, at the cost of an extra line of height; 14AA and F516 are more minimal/compact but I cannot see any craft difference between them.
why.information_hierarchy: In all three the question title is unmistakably the largest/boldest element and reads first within 3 seconds. 14AA and F516 keep the header (# Slack / 外部に出る) on one compact line so nothing above the title competes for attention; D420 splits that into two lines with an icon, which pulls the eye slightly before the title, marginally softening the hierarchy.
why.preview_readability: The body sentence (明日の会議、資料を先に共有します。10月の導入時期の件も入れておきました。) renders with identical size, weight, color and line spacing in all three images — no readability difference detectable.
why.provenance_visibility: The 出所 row (週次同期・田中・10:42 with chevron) is placed identically below the body with the same muted styling in all three — equally visible/unobtrusive in each.
why.screen_occupation: 14AA and F516 use a single-line header (# Slack  外部に出る together), which is visibly more compact top-to-bottom than D420, which stacks '# Slack' and '↗ 外部に出る' on two separate lines, adding roughly one line of extra height for the same content.
why.overall: D420 edges ahead because its label/value weight contrast makes role legibility genuinely clearer at a glance and its warning treatment feels more intentional, even though it costs a bit of vertical space and slightly delays reaching the title. 14AA and F516 are tied and, as far as I can see, visually indistinguishable from each other in this set.

differences: D420's header wraps '# Slack' and '↗ 外部に出る' onto two separate lines with an up-right arrow icon before '外部に出る'; 14AA and F516 keep '# Slack' and '外部に出る' on one line with no icon, just orange text.

D420 renders the 宛先/差出人 values (#sales, あなた) in a visibly bolder weight than their gray labels; in 14AA and F516 the values look like plain/regular weight, distinguished from the labels mainly by color/brightness rather than weight.
D420 therefore occupies slightly more vertical space at the top of the card than 14AA and F516 due to the two-line header.

I could not find any visible difference between 14AA and F516 anywhere in the card (header, title, 宛先/差出人 rows, body text, 出所 row, or buttons) — if a difference exists it is too subtle for me to detect from these renders.
